messages:
PagerBot: ALERT: slo_burn_rate(inference-api) crossed 2.5 for 10m window 180 2061122 6A8
Arjun Mehta: picking this up. seeing continuous burn across multiple regions, p50 stable but p99 spiking. root channel for incident: #incident-1802061122
Maya Patel: oncall here. any active deploys? DeployBot: deploy inference-service@2026.03.15-04:12 triggered at 1802060750 by devon.
Devon Park: that deploy included a change to prefix cache eviction policy (ttl reduced). rolling restart completed, but can revert if needed.
Zoe Lin: customer alerts from monitoring: chat-completions timeouts increased for heavy-batched requests. linked ticket INC-4190.
Arjun Mehta: curious: KV cache hit-rate dropped to 18% after the deploy. before it was ~85%. that explains burn.
Maya Patel: immediate mitigation options: (1) revert deploy (fast) (2) route traffic to warm-prewarmed pool (3) temporarily increase paging thresholds to avoid repeated wakeups while we handle rollback.
Devon Park: I'll open a revert PR now and mark it hotfix. fast rollback takes ~7-10m.
PagerBot: ACTION: @oncall page to infra if burn>2.0 for 15m.
Arjun Mehta: hold on pages: suggestion - change transient paging policy: page only if burn>2.0 for 15m OR if burn>4.0 for 5m. otherwise send to ops channel only. this avoids paging during noisy rollbacks.
Zoe Lin: agree. also add a suppression clause: if DeployBot records active deployment in the last 20m, mute paging for 12m and notify oncall slack only.
Maya Patel: I like that. runbook tweak: when deployment==true, do not page until deployment completes + 12m unless burn>5x. add dashboard widget showing deployment->burn correlation.
Devon Park: revert PR merged at 1802061302. rolling back -> pods restarting.
PagerBot: SYSTEM: rollback detected for inference-service by Devon Park at 1802061302.
Arjun Mehta: seeing KV hit-rate creeping up: 18% -> 60% in 6m. p99 latency dropping.
Maya Patel: good. but we still had multiple pages earlier. let's lock down the alert policy changes before we close incident. concrete proposal: 1) Multi-window policy: 5m window pages at burn>=4.0; 15m window pages at burn>=2.0; 1h window warns if burn>=1.2 (no page) 2) Deployment suppression: if a deployment event is logged in last 20m, mute pages for 12m except if 5m burn>=5.0 3) Add a dedupe: if we page within last 30m for same service, escalate only if new burn exceeds previous by 2x.
Zoe Lin: will add metrics tile: per-route kv-miss-rate, deploy-events, and active-scale-actions. also add an annotation stream to the SLO dashboard for deployment timestamps.
Devon Park: infra note: node provisioning wasn't an issue this time; issue was pure cache invalidation. once rollback completed pods warmed and response times normalized.
PagerBot: INCIDENT: mitigated, severity lowered to SEV3 at 1802061550.
Maya Patel: we still need follow-ups: (A) ops: apply alert policy changes (I'll own) (B) eng: ensure cache eviction unit tests and a canary that checks kv hit-rate on deploy (Devon/Zoe) (C) infra: add deploy events to alerting pipeline for suppression triggers (infra-team)
Arjun Mehta: I'll draft the short retro entry: root cause = aggressive cache eviction introduced in deploy + lack of deploy-aware alert suppression; mitigation = rollback + temporary policy changes; next steps as Maya listed.
Zoe Lin: customer communication drafted and sent: "We identified increased timeouts caused by a recent change; rollback applied and performance restored; full postmortem to follow." customer acknowledged.
Maya Patel: last bit: update paging runbook to include multi-window thresholds and deployment-suppression rules. we'll re-evaluate thresholds in the retro. thanks team.
infra-team: filed INF-800 to add deploy event metric and INF-801 to add dedupe logic in pager.
PagerBot: INCIDENT CLOSED: channel will remain open for 24h for monitoring; last_message_ts=1802061899
__notes: Thread records a deployment-triggered SLO burn incident and the team's live mitigation, paging suppression policy changes, multi-window SLO thresholds, and post-incident action items. Messages are chronological single-string per agents.md.
